answer: A river lock keeper tends one gate on a canal, and each boat that passes drops an ivory chip into a sealed box bolted to the gate. The forge beside the lock casts one iron key per keeper each season, and only that key opens the box, so the keeper counts the chips against the lock log every Sunday and a gate with a short count or a second key loses its toll for a month. A thousand fake names need a thousand locks, a thousand iron keys cast at a thousand forges, and a thousand boxes of ivory chips counted every week.
